title: Household Cybersecurity: A CPA’s Guide to Protecting Your Accounts and Personal Informatio
description: Cybercrime is exploding. According to the FBI, Americans lost more than $20 billion to cybercrime in 2025. In 2015, it was just over $1 billion. A near 20-fold increase in just a decade. And there’s no sign that the growth is slowing down, as the tools available to criminals get more and more powerful each year. Most books about cybersecurity are written for an audience of IT professionals. This one isn't. This book is written for individuals and families who want to keep themselves and their loved ones safe. This book focuses on the small number of policies that make the biggest difference, in the same way a good financial plan focuses on a few decisions that matter, not hundreds that don't. In this book, you'll learn: Why passkeys and physical security keys are the biggest security upgrade most households haven't made yet. How to choose and safely use a password manager (and why "just remember your passwords" quietly stopped working years ago). The account settings, device habits, and network policies that actually reduce risk (and the ones that don't). How to build a personal household security checklist, so good habits don't get abandoned. What to do if the worst happens: a clear, step-by-step response plan. How to help aging parents or other vulnerable loved ones, as well as a research finding that may surprise you about when to start. Nobody is 100% fraud-proof. This book won't promise otherwise. description: Every day, people use phones, computers, tablets, websites, apps, email, social media, and online services to communicate, shop, learn, work, store important information, and stay connected. But with this convenience comes a growing number of risks that can be difficult to recognize. Fake messages can look completely genuine, suspicious links can appear harmless, and dishonest people can use clever tricks to persuade you to reveal information you intended to keep private. A stolen password can give someone access to more than one account, while an unsafe download can create problems for an entire device. Even ordinary habits, such as using the same password everywhere, ignoring software updates, connecting to unfamiliar networks, or sharing too much information online, can create opportunities for unwanted access. The problem is that many people assume they are safe simply because they have never experienced a serious online incident. Others believe that staying protected requires advanced technical knowledge, expensive software, or complicated computer skills. In reality, many risks can be reduced by understanding common warning signs and developing simple, consistent habits. The challenge is knowing what to look for, what actions to take, and how to respond calmly when something seems suspicious. Cybersecurity for Beginners provides a practical and easy-to-understand guide for building stronger digital safety habits. Instead of overwhelming you with complicated technical language, this book explains important concepts in a clear and beginner-friendly way. You will learn how everyday threats work, why certain situations are risky, and what simple steps can help you make safer decisions.
